page: Microsoft Azure E8ds_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 307 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results place the E8ds_v4 consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1287.0 and a multi-core score of 4964.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 415.23 GB/sec, which drops to 49.8 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database operations are supported by a Redis SET throughput of 7.09 million operations per second and a Passmark database score of 2774.19.

While the instance handles standard workloads reliably, it exhibits performance limitations under heavy parallel processing and modern AI workloads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25% of benchmarks at 28.2 GB/sec. Furthermore, LLM inference speeds for a medium 7B model are weak to poor, processing only 14.31 prompt tokens per second and 6.81 text generation tokens per second. Consequently, this server is appropriate for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational databases, and web serving, rather than complex parallel computing or large-scale machine learning inference.
